notes:
I have gathered extensive material from several sources. Let me now compile the verse-by-verse notes, drawing from what these sites say and noting where traditions differ. Here is the commentary:

---

## Revelation 20 – Verse-by-Verse Commentary

### v. 1: *"Then I saw an angel coming down from heaven with the key to the Abyss, holding in his hand a great chain."*

- **The angel is anonymous.** It is not Jesus, nor Michael, nor any high-ranking archangel. This underscores that Satan is not God's equal; a nameless angel, on divine authority, easily subdues him. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-20/)
- **The key and chain symbolize authority and supernatural restraint.** Since Satan is a spiritual being, the "chain" is not literal iron but depicts the angel's God-given power to bind him. Precept Austin notes this is the *de facto* (actual) fulfillment of what Christ accomplished *de jure* (legally) at the cross (Gen. 3:15). (https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-20-commentary)
- **The key of the abyss** was seen earlier at the fifth trumpet (Rev. 9:1), where a "star" (angel) unlocked the pit to release demonic locusts. Here the opposite action occurs: the abyss is locked. (https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-20-commentary)
- **Pulpit Commentary** (amillennial): The angel is a vision-figure; Christ Himself holds "the keys of death and of Hades" (Rev. 1:18). The chain symbolizes the restraint of Satan's power accomplished at the cross. (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/tpc/revelation-20.html)
- **Ellicott** (idealist/amillennial): The key and chain show that the power to bind belongs to "Him who has the keys of death and of Hades." It "is not needful to inquire too curiously" about the angel's identity. (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/revelation-20.html)

### v. 2: *"He seized the dragon, that ancient serpent who is the devil and Satan, and bound him for a thousand years."*

- **The four names** — dragon, ancient serpent, devil, Satan — are identical to Revelation 12:9. They describe his ferocity (dragon), cunning (serpent), slander (devil), and adversarial character (Satan). (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-20/)
- **Premillennial view** (Enduring Word / Guzik, Precept Austin / Garland, MacArthur / GTY): This is a literal, future binding at Christ's Second Coming. Satan is rendered completely inactive for a literal thousand years. Precept Austin argues at length that if Satan were bound now, "his chain is too long," citing numerous NT passages (1 Pet. 5:8; 2 Cor. 4:3-4; Eph. 2:2; etc.) showing Satan remains active in this age. (https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-20-commentary) (https://www.gty.org/sermons/66-73/the-coming-earthly-kingdom-of-the-lord-jesus-christ-part-1)
- **Amillennial/Spiritual view** (Pulpit Commentary): The binding took place when Christ bruised the serpent's head by His redeeming work. "Christ was manifested that he might destroy the works of the devil" (1 John 3:8); "Now shall the prince of this world be cast out" (John 12:31). The binding limits Satan's power *in relation to the godly* — Christians need not fear him. (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/tpc/revelation-20.html)
- **Ellicott**: The binding is achieved by Christ (Matt. 12:29; Col. 2:15). The thousand years is not to be understood literally; it was the length Rabbis fixed for Messiah's kingdom and symbolizes a lengthened period. (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/revelation-20.html)

### v. 3: *"And he threw him into the Abyss, shut it, and sealed it over him, so that he could not deceive the nations until the thousand years were complete. After that, he must be released for a brief period of time."*

- **Threefold security**: Satan is bound, shut up (locked in), and sealed. Precept Austin notes the Greek word for "sealed" (*esphragisen*) is the same as sealing elsewhere in Revelation (7:3-8; 10:4) indicating complete effectiveness. (https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-20-commentary)
- **Satan's main weapon is deception.** Since he is bound "that he should deceive the nations no more," the truth of God's Word is the most potent defense against him. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-20/)
- **Guzik argues that Satan is *not* bound in this way today**, since Peter says he "walks about like a roaring lion" (1 Pet. 5:8) and deception continues. The binding is future. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-20/)
- **Pulpit Commentary** (amillennial): The "thousand years" expresses *quality*, not a period of time. It means Satan is *completely* bound — for believers. The "loosing for a little season" (same phrase as Rev. 6:11) means Satan is simultaneously loosed among the ungodly during this present age. The binding and loosing are contemporaneous, not sequential; "after this" is subordination of the secondary fact to the primary, not chronological sequence. (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/tpc/revelation-20.html)
- **Ellicott**: The sealing reminds us of the sealing of Christ's tomb (Matt. 27:66). The exact moment of binding need not be fixed to any one incident; it may be gradual in fulfillment. The duration is symbolic — "it is not to be understood literally any more than the other numbers in the book." (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/revelation-20.html)

### v. 4: *"Then I saw the thrones, and those seated on them had been given authority to judge. And I saw the souls of those who had been beheaded for their testimony of Jesus and for the word of God, and those who had not worshiped the beast or its image, and had not received its mark... And they came to life and reigned with Christ for a thousand years."*

- **Who sits on the thrones?** Possibly the 24 elders (the Church, Rev. 4:4), the apostles (Matt. 19:28), or the whole company of saints (1 Cor. 6:2-3). Precept Austin identifies them as overcomers who received Jesus' promises to Thyatira and Laodicea (Rev. 2:26-27; 3:21). (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-20/) (https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-20-commentary)
- **Two groups are specially named**: (1) Tribulation martyrs beheaded for their testimony, and (2) those who refused the beast's mark. Guzik says they are specially mentioned for encouragement, while not excluding other saints. "Beheaded" (*pepelekismenōn*) literally means "executed with an axe," but is a broader term for execution. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-20/) (https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-20-commentary)
- **"They came to life and reigned"** — Premillennial view: This is a literal, bodily resurrection of believers who reign with Christ on earth during the Millennium. Precept Austin notes the "souls" are "once disembodied (Rev. 6:9), but here clearly resurrected." (https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-20-commentary)
- **Amillennial/Spiritual view** (Pulpit Commentary): This describes Christians' position *in this life*. They "sit upon thrones" — i.e., they reign with Christ spiritually. "Judgment was given unto them" means by their conduct the world is judged and condemned. The "living and reigning" is the "first resurrection" — a spiritual rising from sin to gospel life (John 5:24; 1 John 3:14). (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/tpc/revelation-20.html)
- **Ellicott** (idealist): The thrones are shared by *all the faithful*, not just martyrs. They "reign, they judge, they live; the true and full powers of life are seen to be theirs." The saints exercise judicial power now: "Those who lived for God, and refused the mark of earthliness, reign and judge us in our worldliness and weakness." (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/revelation-20.html)
- **Reformed/Historic Premillennial** (Piper/Desiring God): Piper identifies as premillennial — Christ returns *before* the Millennium. He says "a lot hangs on what you make of 'the first resurrection.'" He believes it refers to the resurrection at Christ's Second Coming, and the Millennium begins then. (https://www.desiringgod.org/interviews/how-soon-is-christs-return)
- **Baptist/Dispensational Premillennial** (MacArthur/GTY): The chronology of Revelation demands premillennialism — Christ returns in chapter 19, the Kingdom is in chapter 20, and the eternal state is in chapter 21. "A normal chronology and a simple literal interpretation yields premillennialism." (https://www.gty.org/sermons/66-74/the-coming-earthly-kingdom-of-the-lord-jesus-christ-part-2)

### v. 5: *"The rest of the dead did not come back to life until the thousand years were complete. This is the first resurrection."*

- **Premillennial view**: "The rest of the dead" are the unsaved, who are not raised until after the Millennium for the Great White Throne judgment. The "first resurrection" is the bodily resurrection of the righteous, occurring in phases (Christ the firstfruits, the Church at the Rapture, OT and Tribulation saints at the Second Coming). (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-20/) (https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-20-commentary)
- **Amillennial view** (Pulpit): "The rest of the dead" refers to OT saints and godly people before Christ's atonement who could not "live" in John's high sense (John 1:4) — not having known Christ. Christ's redeeming work placed them on a level with Christians (Heb. 11:39-40). The "first resurrection" is spiritual regeneration. (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/tpc/revelation-20.html)
- **Ellicott**: The word "resurrection" need not be literal. NT writers use it figuratively (Eph. 2:1; 5:14; John 5:24-25). He notes that if the saints have glorified resurrection bodies while "men and women still in the natural body" inhabit the earth, it creates a difficulty. The first resurrection is spiritual. (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/revelation-20.html)

### v. 6: *"Blessed and holy are those who share in the first resurrection! The second death has no power over them, but they will be priests of God and of Christ, and will reign with Him for a thousand years."*

- **One of seven beatitudes in Revelation.** "Blessed and holy" — they are blessed because they "shall be priests of God and of Christ, and shall reign with Him," and holy because they are saints (*hagioi*) who "washed their robes … in the blood of the Lamb" (Rev. 7:14). (https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-20-commentary)
- **"Second death has no power"**: Christ promised the overcomer at Smyrna — the persecuted, martyred church — they would not be hurt by the second death (Rev. 2:11). The second death is the lake of fire (Rev. 20:14; 21:8). (https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-20-commentary)
- **Ellicott**: The second death is "spiritual rather than physical." "It is not the life of the body which protects the life of the spirit; it is the living and believing in God which protects from the second death" (John 11:26). The priesthood and reign are the "priesthood of life" — they offered themselves as living sacrifices. (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/revelation-20.html)

### vv. 7–8: *"When the thousand years are complete, Satan will be released from his prison, and will go out to deceive the nations in the four corners of the earth—Gog and Magog—to assemble them for battle. Their number is like the sand of the seashore."*

- **Why release Satan?** Guzik explains: Even after a thousand years of perfect environment (no Satan, no crime, peace, righteousness), mankind still rebels. This demonstrates that human sinfulness comes from within, not just from environment. It also displays Satan's eternal depravity. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-20/)
- **Who rebels?** Those who survived the Great Tribulation, entered the Millennium in natural bodies, and their descendants. Infants born during the Millennium live to its end, and outward conformity to Christ's rule does not equal inward faith. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-20/)
- **Gog and Magog**: Names drawn from Ezekiel 38–39. Guzik says the Ezekiel battle seems distinct — likely occurring before or during the Tribulation — while this final battle is at the end of the Millennium. John borrows the names as symbols. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-20/)
- **Ellicott**: Gog and Magog are *figurative* names for all hostile nations. In rabbinical books they described nations rising against the Messiah. Magog (Gen. 10:2) is associated with northern/Scythian invaders; the names represent "the great hosts of the nations … who would break forth into uncalled-for hostility against the people of the Lord." (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/revelation-20.html)
- **Pulpit Commentary** (amillennial): The release is contemporaneous with the binding — Satan is "loosed" among the ungodly throughout the church age. Gog and Magog denote the ungodly people of the world among whom Satan still exercises power. The "war" (Greek has the article: *the* war) is the ongoing war of Revelation 16:14 and 19:19 — a prolonged war lasting throughout life, not a single battle. (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/tpc/revelation-20.html)
- **MacArthur (GTY)** describes this as "the revolt of society" — a final, vast rebellion crushed instantly. (https://www.gty.org/sermons/66-73/the-coming-earthly-kingdom-of-the-lord-jesus-christ-part-1)

### v. 9: *"And they marched across the broad expanse of the earth and surrounded the camp of the saints and the beloved city. But fire came down from heaven and consumed them."*

- **No real battle**: The fight is over before it begins. "Fire came down from God out of heaven and devoured them." Guzik says we should not even call this a battle. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-20/)
- **"The beloved city"** is Jerusalem — the "capital" of Christ's millennial administration. The "camp of the saints" may be glorified saints reigning with Christ or earth-dwelling believers. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-20/)
- **Ellicott**: The beloved city is "the figure of the true spiritual Zion and Jerusalem which has been faithful to her king." The fire from heaven recalls the destruction of Sodom (Gen. 19:24), Elijah's fire upon his enemies (2 Kings 1:9-14), and fire from the tabernacle (Num. 16:35). The imagery is figurative, though not empty — "Christ will thoroughly purge His floor" (Matt. 3:12). (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/revelation-20.html)
- **Pulpit Commentary**: "The beloved city" is the Church of God, of which Jerusalem is always a type in the Apocalypse (Rev. 3:12; 21:2, 10). The fire portrays God aiding and protecting His Church even while on earth — a foretaste of the lake of fire. (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/tpc/revelation-20.html)

### v. 10: *"And the devil who had deceived them was thrown into the lake of fire and sulfur, into which the beast and the false prophet had already been thrown. There they will be tormented day and night forever and ever."*

- **Eternal, conscious punishment**: Guzik and Walvoord (as quoted by Guzik) emphasize that "forever and ever" (*to the ages of ages*) is the strongest possible Greek phrasing for everlasting duration. The beast and false prophet were cast into the lake of fire a thousand years earlier (Rev. 19:20) and are still there — arguing against annihilationism. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-20/)
- **Ellicott**: The devil, previously cast from heaven (Rev. 12:9) and bound in the abyss, is now flung into the flaming lake. "They (i.e., the devil, the wild beast, and the false prophet) are tormented unto the ages of ages." (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/revelation-20.html)
- **Pulpit Commentary**: This verse completes the series of visions begun in Revelation 12 — the origin, progress, and final end of evil. The torment is final. (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/tpc/revelation-20.html)

### v. 11: *"Then I saw a great white throne and the One seated on it. Earth and heaven fled from His presence, and no place was found for them."*

- **The Great White Throne**: "Great" in status, power, and authority; "white" in purity and holiness; a "throne" in kingly sovereignty. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-20/)
- **Who sits on it?** Guzik says the Judge is Jesus (John 5:22-27) or the fullness of the Triune God. Ellicott says throughout Revelation, God is "Him that sitteth upon the throne" (Rev. 4:3; 5:1), but the Son sits with the Father (Rev. 3:21; Matt. 25:31-32). (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-20/) (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/revelation-20.html)
- **Heaven and earth flee**: No place to hide — there is absolutely no escape from this judgment. Ellicott cautions against reading physical catastrophe into "confessedly poetical" language, though "revolution must precede renewal" (Rev. 21:1). (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-20/) (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/revelation-20.html)
- **Premillennial view**: Most Bible scholars believe Christians will never appear before this throne — our sins were already judged in Jesus at the cross. Christians face the *judgment seat of Christ* (2 Cor. 5:10), not the Great White Throne. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-20/)
- **Pulpit Commentary** (differing slightly): The dead *include* good and bad (Matt. 25:31-33). "All the dead, good and bad" stand before God; this is the general resurrection. Those who "would not voluntarily share in the first resurrection [spiritual regeneration] are compelled to share in the second [the general resurrection unto judgment]." (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/tpc/revelation-20.html)

### vv. 12–13: *"And I saw the dead, great and small, standing before the throne. And there were open books, and one of them was the Book of Life. And the dead were judged according to their deeds, as recorded in the books. The sea gave up its dead, and Death and Hades gave up their dead, and each one was judged according to his deeds."*

- **Not a trial but a sentencing**. The facts are in; this is the judgment of condemnation. Works are judged to determine the *degree* of eternal punishment, not to determine salvation — those present have already rejected God's grace. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-20/)
- **Piper (Desiring God / Reformed Baptist)**: Both believers and unbelievers face this judgment. The "books" contain the record of deeds; the "Book of Life" secures salvation for those written in it. Being in the Book of Life is based on Christ's being slain (Rev. 13:8), not on deeds. But the deeds recorded in the books serve as *public confirmation* of faith and union with Christ. "No one is saved on the basis of his works. But everyone who is saved does new works." (https://www.desiringgod.org/articles/what-will-the-final-judgment-mean-for-you)
- **"The sea gave up its dead"**: The sea represents the place of unburied bodies; the emphasis is on the *universal* character of judgment — no one is excluded, no matter how they died or were disposed of. (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-20/)
- **Pulpit Commentary**: "Sea" may also typify the ungodly nations — those spiritually dead but physically alive at the judgment, alongside those physically dead. "Death and Hades" are personified: Death seizes, and Hades (the grave/underworld) guards the seized. (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/tpc/revelation-20.html)

### vv. 14–15: *"Then Death and Hades were thrown into the lake of fire. This is the second death—the lake of fire. And if anyone was found whose name was not written in the Book of Life, he was thrown into the lake of fire."*

- **Death and Hades personified** are destroyed — the very result and realm of sin are eliminated forever. This fulfills 1 Corinthians 15:26: "The last enemy that shall be abolished is death." (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-20/)
- **"Second death"**: Not mere physical dying, but eternal separation from God in the lake of fire. It is the destiny of all not found in the Book of Life. (https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-20-commentary)
- **Pulpit Commentary**: John never uses the phrase "first death," but it corresponds to physical death — the natural result of the spiritually dead state into which humanity is born since the Fall. The "first resurrection" is spiritual regeneration; the "second resurrection" is the general resurrection of all. (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/tpc/revelation-20.html)
- **Piper**: Verse 15 implies that being in the Book of Life ensures one will not perish. The names there are "not saved on the basis of their deeds" but on the basis of Christ's being slain (Rev. 13:8). (https://www.desiringgod.org/articles/what-will-the-final-judgment-mean-for-you)

## Summary: Where Protestant Traditions Differ on Revelation 20

**The three main millennial views** represented across the examined sources:

| View | Teachers/Traditions Represented | Key Distinctive |
|---|---|---|
| **Premillennialism** (Christ returns *before* the 1,000 years) | David Guzik/Enduring Word (Pentecostal-charismatic), John MacArthur/GTY (Baptist-dispensational), Precept Austin/Garland (evangelical-dispensational), John Piper/Desiring God (Reformed Baptist, historic premillennial) | A literal future 1,000-year earthly reign of Christ; Satan is literally bound; the first resurrection is bodily. Takes Revelation 19→20→21 as chronological. |
| **Amillennialism** (no future literal millennium; we are in it now, spiritually) | Pulpit Commentary, Ellicott's Commentary (Anglican-idealist), many Reformed and Lutheran traditions | The 1,000 years symbolizes the entire church age. Satan was bound at the cross (in relation to believers). The first resurrection is spiritual regeneration. |
| **Postmillennialism** (Christ returns *after* a golden age brought by the church) | Spurgeon (historic premillennial with postmillennial sympathies — cited by Guzik looking for "the future triumph of Christ over the whole world"); some Reformed traditions | The gospel triumphs progressively; the Millennium is a future golden age before Christ returns. Not separately detailed in the fetched materials. |

**On the binding of Satan**:
- **Premillennial**: Future, complete, literal binding — Satan cannot deceive *at all*. Satan is *not* bound now (1 Pet. 5:8; 2 Cor. 4:3-4). (https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-20-commentary)
- **Amillennial** (Pulpit, Ellicott): Satan was bound at the cross — completely, for believers. The binding and loosing are contemporaneous; he is bound toward the godly and loosed among the ungodly. (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/tpc/revelation-20.html)

**On the first resurrection**:
- **Premillennial**: A literal, bodily resurrection of the righteous at Christ's return (with phases: Church at Rapture, OT/Tribulation saints at Second Coming). (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-20/)
- **Amillennial**: Spiritual regeneration — the new birth (John 5:24-25; Eph. 2:1). The "rest of the dead" who "lived not" are OT saints who could not know Christ's life before the atonement. (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/tpc/revelation-20.html) (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/revelation-20.html)

**On the Great White Throne judgment**:
- **Premillennial** (Guzik): Only the unsaved dead appear here; believers face the separate "judgment seat of Christ." (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-20/)
- **Piper** (Reformed): All dead, believers and unbelievers, stand before this throne. Believers are not condemned — their deeds serve as public confirmation of faith. (https://www.desiringgod.org/articles/what-will-the-final-judgment-mean-for-you)
- **Pulpit**: All dead, "good and bad," are judged; this is the general resurrection. (https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/tpc/revelation-20.html)

## Other Views (Well-Known but Not Fully Accessible)

Due to search limits, I was unable to retrieve detailed pages from the following sources. However, based on what is widely known and briefly surfaced:

- **Roman Catholic view** (newadvent.org, catholic.com): The *Catechism of the Catholic Church* (§676) follows an amillennial reading. The "millennium" is the present reign of Christ in His Church. The "first resurrection" is baptismal regeneration. The Church has officially rejected chiliasm (premillennialism) since Augustine.
- **Eastern Orthodox view** (oca.org): Orthodox theology generally follows an amillennial understanding. The 1,000 years is symbolic of the Church age; Christ reigns now through the Church. The Orthodox reject literal earthly millennialism (chiliasm), which was condemned at the Second Ecumenical Council (Constantinople, 381) by the addition of "whose kingdom shall have no end" to the Creed.
- **Lutheran view** (lcms.org, 1517.org): The Lutheran Confessions (Augsburg Confession, Article XVII) explicitly condemn "the opinion that before the resurrection of the dead the godly shall take possession of the kingdom of the world, the ungodly being everywhere suppressed." Lutherans are amillennial.
- **Methodist/Wesleyan view** (wesley.nnu.edu, seedbed.com): Wesleyan tradition has historically been amillennial or postmillennial, emphasizing the spread of holiness and social transformation, though some modern Wesleyans hold to premillennialism.
- **Modern scholarship** (bibleodyssey.org, netbible.org): Generally treats Revelation as apocalyptic literature using symbolic imagery. The NET Bible notes likely treat the 1,000 years symbolically and note the dependence on Ezekiel 38–39 for the Gog-Magog imagery. These pages were not fetched.
